issues.evidence: csv_analytics.py -o /nonexistent/x.json -> FileNotFoundError traceback, rc=1 (A/csv_analytics.py:190 open() outside try)
issues.summary: Unwritable --output path crashes with an uncaught traceback instead of a clean error.
Minor lint findings (long lines, zip without strict).
A single non-numeric cell in a numeric column silently nulls every numeric stat for that column.

issues.evidence: header 'id, age' with --columns age -> 'error: unknown column: age' (headers not stripped)
issues.summary: Header names with whitespace after commas are not normalized, so natural column names are rejected.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a unit-test suite and a stricter exit-code/error contract, which hints at a more process-driven workflow, but the signal is weak.

notes: Both sides passed all 21 black-box probes (stats, even/odd median, numeric/string/AND filters, selection, JSON export, quoting, missing/ragged data, error paths). Differences only showed up in edge cases I probed by hand: A crashes with a traceback on an unwritable output path; B nulls all stats for mixed columns and doesn't strip header whitespace. A has extra features (multi-file, stdin, table output, ~= filter, --rows) but no tests; B has 8 passing unittest tests. Bandit reported nothing for either side. Probes ran with python3.11 (system python3 is 3.9, which lacks sys.stdlib_module_names).
